title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 10
paragraphs: Thus he advised them, and they at once took his words to heart. Without saying a word to the envoys from the cities, while it was still night they sent out five thousand Spartans, with no fewer than seven Helots to attend each man, appointing Pausanias son of Cleombrotos to lead them. The leadership actually belonged to Pleistarchos son of Leonidas; but he was still a boy, and Pausanias was his guardian and cousin. For Cleombrotos, father of Pausanias and son of Anaxandrides, was no longer alive: not long after he led home from the Isthmus the army that had built the wall, he died. The reason Cleombrotos led the army home from the Isthmus was this: as he was offering sacrifice for fighting against the Persian, the sun was darkened in the sky. Pausanias chose as his fellow commander Euryanax son of Dorieos, a man of the same royal house.
